summary: Friedrich Bollensen was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1827–1833) and Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald (~1830–1833). He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, the Main Pedagogical Institute (1846), and Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).
Friedrich Brockhaus held professorships at the University of Jena (~1868), the University of Basel (~1868–1871), the University of Marburg (~1871–1872), and Kiel University (~1872–1895).

Friedrich Carl Andreas worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, having studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1866–1868). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1896–1903) and the University of Göttingen (~1903–1930).

Friedrich Christian Diez was a linguist who studied at the University of Giessen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1811–1813) and at the University of Göttingen (~1813–1816). He held a post at the University of Bonn from ~1822 to 1876.

Friedrich Creuzer was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at the universities of Tübingen (~1789–1791) and Jena (~1791–1794), holding posts at Marburg (~1800–1804), Leiden (1809), and Heidelberg (~1804–1845).

Linguist and historian Friedrich Delitzsch studied at Leipzig (~1868–1872) under Windisch, Fleischer, Brockhaus, and Curtius, and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1872–1873) under Dillmann. He held posts at the University of Breslau (~1893–1899) and Berlin (~1899–1920).
Friedrich Ernst August Krause was a sinologist who studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1900–1903). He later held a post at Heidelberg University from ~1923 to 1935.

Linguist and historian Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker studied at the University of Giessen (~1801–1803). He held academic posts at Giessen (~1808–1816), the University of Göttingen (~1816–1819), and the University of Bonn (~1819–1861).

Haag, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held posts at the Cathedral School of Tallinn, Zurich, Kantonsschule Schaffhausen, Gymnasium Burgdorf, and the University of Bern (1887; 1891–1906).

Friedrich Heiler was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Munich (~1912–1917). He taught at Munich in 1918, joined the University of Marburg in 1920, and led the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962).

Friedrich Hirth, a sinologist and historian, studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald (~1865–1869). He served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) and held the Dean Lung Professorship of Chinese at Columbia University (1902).
Friedrich Kurschat was a linguist who studied at the University of Königsberg from ~1836 to 1840 and subsequently held a post there from ~1840 to 1883.
Linguist Friedrich Leo studied at Göttingen and Bonn under Hermann Usener. He held posts at Bonn, Kiel, Rostock, Strasbourg, and the University of Göttingen (1889–1914).

Friedrich Majer was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Jena (~1789–1792) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1792–1803). He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Jena.

Max Müller studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under Brockhaus, Bopp, Schelling, and Burnouf, and under Wilson. An Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar, he held posts at Oxford from 1850 to 1900 and at All Souls College.

Linguist and Indologist Friedrich Müller studied at Vienna under Boller, at Göttingen, and at Tübingen. He worked at the K.K. Hof- und Staatsdruckerei, Vienna University Library, and Austrian National Library, becoming professor at Vienna in 1869.
Friedrich Nietzsche, active in philosophy and linguistics, studied at Bonn and Leipzig under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl. He served on the faculty at the University of Basel from 1869 to 1878.

Friedrich Otto Schrader was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1899–1902). He directed the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1905–1916) and served as Professor of Indology at Kiel University from 1921.
Friedrich Ottomar Eduard Wilhelm held academic posts at the University of Freiburg from ~1910 to 1911 and at the University of Munich from ~1913 to 1939.

Rückert, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Würzburg and Heidelberg, and under Hammer-Purgstall and Bopp. He held posts at Jena (1811), as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826), and as professor of Arabic at Berlin (1841–1849).
